posts.author: vforge
posts.content_md: Another materials question: in several of the old acrylamide/acrylate photopolymer formulations, they used methylene blue to sensitize the plates to HeNe wavelengths. I'd like to try some of those formulations, but instead sensitize the plates for dpss green at 532nm. Is there a "drop in" replacement for methylene blue that works at a green wavelength, like a methylene orange or something? For that matter, a methylene red would be nice to work with blue or violet lasers.

posts.content_md:

I'd like to try some of those formulations, but instead sensitize the plates for dpss green at 532nm. For that matter, a methylene red would be nice to work with blue or violet lasers.

The dyes discussed in the recent thread here -

[http://holographyforum.org/phpBB2/viewtopic.php?t=3957](http://holographyforum.org/phpBB2/viewtopic.php?t=3957)

are all about acting as free radical generators although the thread is specifically about reducing dichromate to Cr111 for gelatin, so if you have TEA present you decolorize the dye by a free radical mechanism and that can then go on to polymerize acrylamide with methylene bis acrylamide as

crosslinker. Cheap Acrylic acid works fine too as an alternative to acrylamide.

jeff

posts.author: jeff-blyth
posts.content_md:
> **letgo21cn:** vforge wrote:Another materials question: in several of the old acrylamide/acrylate photopolymer formulations, they used methylene blue to sensitize the plates to HeNe wavelengths. I'd like to try some of those formulations, but instead sensitize the plates for dpss green at 532nm. Is there a "drop in" replacement for methylene blue that works at a green wavelength, like a methylene orange or something? For that matter, a methylene red would be nice to work with blue or violet lasers.as i know, Ciba Igacure 784 works very well with 514.5nm and the Erythrosin B as an sensitizer with TEA is another chioce.

I have discovered since vforge's original posting that Safranine "O" works exactly as a drop in replacement for MB , it has good water solubility and

is a cationic dye like MB ie it is a chloride salt whereas erythrosin is an anionic dye ie you buy it as the sodium salt.

So the significance of this is that you can get panchromatic sensitivity

because Safranine 'O' (let's call it SO)gives photosensitivity to the 532nm region and you can mix it with MB OK. Whereas MB mixed with erythrosin B can cause problems with their opposite charges.

jeff
